source_evidence.observation: A random variable is called sub-gaussian when it satisfies one of the equivalent properties (i)-(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2, and its sub-gaussian norm is defined by ||X||_{psi_2} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}.
The source says that every sub-gaussian random variable X satisfies ||X||_{L^p} <= C ||X||_{psi_2} sqrt(p) for every p >= 1, where C > 0 is an absolute constant.

The moment condition underlying Equation (2.15) is ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) <= K_2 sqrt(p) for every p >= 1; the proposition states that its parameter and the parameters in the other sub-gaussian characterizations differ by at most an absolute constant factor.
The enclosing restatement adds that, up to absolute constant factors, ||X||_{psi_2} is the smallest possible scale that makes each displayed characterization valid.

binders: p, a real number with p >= 1
C > 0, an absolute numerical constant independent of X and p
hypotheses: X is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6, equivalently X satisfies one of properties (i)-(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2.
definitions_and_conventions: An absolute constant is a universal numerical constant, so C does not depend on X or p.
implicit_context: Expectation and the L^p norm are taken with respect to the probability law on the underlying probability space of X.
No assumption E[X] = 0 is imposed for Equation (2.15); the mean-zero condition in the surrounding display applies only to the MGF bound (2.16).
Equation (2.15) is the moment-growth component of the restatement of Proposition 2.5.2 in terms of the sub-gaussian norm.
The sentence after the displayed bounds records an up-to-absolute-constant optimality characterization of ||X||_{psi_2}; it is surrounding context rather than text inside Equation (2.15).

details: There is one universal absolute constant C for the bound, and the inequality holds for every sub-gaussian X and every real p >= 1.
The constant may change between comparable formulations in the surrounding text, but it cannot depend on X or p.
The dependence on the moment order is sqrt(p), not p or another power.
The scale is the sub-gaussian norm ||X||_{psi_2}, so the inequality is homogeneous under scalar rescaling of X.
The bound covers the full range p >= 1.
Neither centering nor independence from any other random variable is required.
The displayed inequality is derived from the equivalence of the tail, moment, and exponential-square characterizations in Proposition 2.5.2.
The subsequent optimality sentence is only up to absolute constant factors and does not specify an exact best numerical C.

undebatable_constraints: The subject is an arbitrary sub-gaussian random variable X; Equation (2.15) does not require X to have mean zero.
The moment exponent p ranges over every real p >= 1.
The left-hand side is the L^p norm (E|X|^p)^(1/p).
The right-hand side is an absolute constant times ||X||_{psi_2} times sqrt(p).
The psi_2 norm uses the normalization threshold E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2.
The constant C is universal and independent of both X and p.
Equation (2.15) is an upper bound; it does not state equality with C ||X||_{psi_2} sqrt(p) or give an exact numerical value for C.

ambiguities.issue: The source denotes several universal constants in the surrounding display by the same letter C without fixing numerical values.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 16, printed page 27, the sentence 'Here C, c > 0 are absolute constants' following Equations (2.14)-(2.16).
ambiguities.impact: Faithfulness requires existence of a universal positive constant with the stated dependence, not a particular numerical constant or literal identity with constants used elsewhere.

ambiguities.issue: The sentence after Equation (2.16) gives an up-to-constant optimality statement for each displayed characterization, but that sentence is not part of the displayed Equation (2.15) itself.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 16, printed page 27, the 'Moreover, up to absolute constant factors' sentence immediately after Equation (2.16).
ambiguities.impact: For the exact Equation (2.15) anchor, the mandatory conclusion is the forward moment upper bound; the optimality characterization should be retained as enclosing context and should only become an additional target conclusion if the audit scope explicitly includes that following sentence.

contracts.contract_plain_english: There is a universal numerical constant C such that any sub-gaussian real random variable X has moments growing at most like the square root of their order: for every real p >= 1, (E|X|^p)^(1/p) is at most C times ||X||_{psi_2} times sqrt(p). Here ||X||_{psi_2} is defined using the exponential-square threshold E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2. No centering or independence assumption is needed. The surrounding text says this moment characterization determines the sub-gaussian scale up to universal constant factors, but Equation (2.15) itself is the stated upper bound.
